messages:
Sam (Sales): Quick heads-up — EuroFin wants a POC with strict EU-only data residency for inference + embeddings. They also want the full subprocessor list and confirmation that failover stays inside EU. Can presales/ops/legal chime in? cc @Akash (Presales) @Maya (Security)

Akash (Presales): Short summary: we can keep the data plane in EU for hosted by tenant pinning or via Dedicated; Private gives full control. Need to confirm whether control-plane traffic (metadata, orchestration) also must remain in EU — that changes timeline/cost. Which requirement did they state exactly?

Sam (Sales): They said: "data at rest and in transit within EU" and prefer the control plane to also be in EU; they asked for an attestation. Also asked whether monitoring/logging or any subprocessors send traffic outside EU.

Ellie (Ops): We have an up-to-date subprocessors CSV (link: https://internal.redwood/ops/subprocessors.csv). For hosted EU tenants we primarily run on eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Third-party services: Datadog (has EU partition opt-in), Sentry (EU option), and cloud provider-managed KMS if not BYO. I can share which components talk to non-EU endpoints.

Maya (Security): FYI default telemetry pipelines go to the US unless we enable EU partitions. For POC we can enable EU-only telemetry and disable nonessential forwarding. I'll pull SOC2/ISO certs and prepare a brief attestation template for residency. :ok_hand:

Ben (Sales): How does failover behave? If eu-west-1 loses capacity, do we fail to eu-central-1 only, or could it default to us-east? Customer wants EU-only failover.

Akash (Presales): We can set an EU-only routing policy for the POC. Example config we can offer to the customer:

```
routing_policy:
  primary_region: eu-west-1
  fallback_regions:
    - eu-central-1
  region_failover_policy: eu-only
  data_plane_geofence: EU
  control_plane_preference: eu (optional/enterprise)
```

Note: Hosted standard control plane currently spans regions and may include US control services; enabling a dedicated EU control plane is available as an enterprise opt-in and takes ~2–3 weeks to provision.

ops-bot: Provision request created: PR-4821 (eu-controlplane-trial). ETA ~14 days.

Ellie (Ops): Cost/ops note: EU control plane + BYO-KMS -> POC cost + ~30% and needs customer KMS config (we support Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS in region). If they want Datadog EU partition we'll need their Datadog org id for remap.

Sam (Sales): Customer says they have Azure Key Vault in eu-north and want BYO-KMS. Next steps I propose: 1) Ops: share precise subprocessors CSV + any opt-in steps for EU partitions 2) Security: attach SOC2/ISO docs and prepare residency attestation wording 3) Presales: produce routing config + POC cost delta and timeline 4) Legal: signoff on attestation & subprocessor list

Maya (Security): On it. I'll DM Sam the certs and draft attestation by EOD. Also flag for ops: Datadog EU opt-in requires remap, will need customer's org id.

Ben (Sales): I'll update the dealroom with "EU-control-plane opt-in required" and the cost delta.

Sam (Sales): Great — thanks everyone. If ops/legal need anything from EuroFin directly (contractual language, point of contact, KMS ARN), I'll collect that today and post here.

Ellie (Ops): I'll attach the detailed subprocessor CSV and a short checklist for the EU POC steps in this thread when PR-4821 lands.

Sam (Sales): Thanks — leaving this open here for follow-ups. :pray:
